## Questions before you start.

Straight answers on the free audit, who does the work and how projects are priced.

Still have a question?

Ask the senior strategist who would run your program.

[(800) 618-6053](tel:+18006186053)

### Is the audit really free?

Yes. The audit is free and carries no obligation. A senior strategist reviews your site, search visibility, AI answer presence and tracking, then sends back the issues, the fixes ranked by revenue impact and what we would do first. You keep the findings whether or not you hire us.

### Who does the work?

Senior strategists and specialists do the work. The people you meet on the first call are the people who plan, build and report on your program across SEO, AI search, web, paid media and email. There are no junior handoffs and no account-manager layer between you and the team.

### Do you work outside Atlanta?

Yes. NativeCode is based in Atlanta, with an office in Norcross, and works with businesses across the United States. Most work runs remotely inside your own tools and accounts, with video calls for planning and reviews. Clients in metro Atlanta can also meet in person when that helps.

### Can you work with our in-house team?

Yes. We can run the whole program, build alongside your marketing, product and engineering teams, or advise and review work your team runs. We work inside your Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Shopify, Webflow and email platform accounts, so the work and the data stay with you.

### How is pricing set?

Every engagement is scoped after the free audit. You get a written scope, timeline and price before any work starts, based on the channels involved, the size of your site and how much your own team handles. Growth programs, projects and advisory work are each scoped separately.

About NativeCode

# One senior team for search, web, creative and growth.

NativeCode is an Atlanta-based digital marketing and engineering firm that runs SEO, AI search, web design and development, paid media, email and creative as one program for brands nationwide. The people who plan the work are the people who do it, and every program is reported against revenue.

[Start a project](https://www.nativecode.ai/company/contact) [See services](https://www.nativecode.ai/#services)

How we work

## How does NativeCode work?

Search, AI discovery and paid channels change every year. What lasts is clear architecture, honest measurement and a team that owns the outcome.

01

### Senior-led

Experienced practitioners run every engagement. No account-manager layer between you and the people doing the work.

02

### One program

Strategy, execution and reporting treated as one system, so search, ads, email and the website pull in the same direction.

03

### An extension of your team

We work with founders, marketing leaders, product and engineering, inside your tools and your planning cycle.

FAQ

## What should you know before you reach out?

### How much does it cost to work with NativeCode?

It depends on scope. After a free audit or a discovery call, a senior strategist sends a written proposal with the scope, timeline and price before any work starts. SEO and AI search programs, paid media, email and web builds are each scoped to your goals, site and team. Share your budget range in the form and we will shape the proposal around it.

### Do you work with companies outside Atlanta?

Yes. NativeCode is based in Atlanta, with an office in Norcross, and works with teams across the United States and in other countries. Most work runs remotely inside your own tools and accounts, with video calls for planning and reviews. Clients in metro Atlanta can also meet in person when that helps.

### What should I include in my message?

Include your goals, the channels you run today, rough traffic or revenue figures if you can share them, and any deadline or launch date. Links to your site, your current reports and the platforms you use, such as Shopify, Webflow, GA4 or Klaviyo, help us come to the first call prepared with a point of view.

### Can you work inside our existing accounts?

Yes. We build in your Google Ads, Meta, GA4, Search Console, Shopify, Webflow and email platform accounts, so the work and the data stay yours. Access is scoped to what the engagement needs and is read-only where possible. Our Security and trust page explains how we handle accounts, devices and client information.

### I am an existing client. Where do I go?

Email your project lead directly for anything about an active engagement. If you are not sure who that is, write to hello@nativecode.ai with your company name in the subject line and we will route it to the right person. For security or vendor-risk questions, email security@nativecode.ai instead.

# Security and Trust

Source: https://www.nativecode.ai/security (updated 2026-11-16)

Security and trust

# Your systems stay yours.

NativeCode works with the least access an engagement needs. Client systems stay under client control unless access is expressly granted, and this page says plainly what we do, what we never touch, and what we are not certified for, so security and procurement teams can review us quickly.

[Contact security](mailto:security@nativecode.ai) [Request documentation](mailto:security@nativecode.ai?subject=Security%20Documentation%20Request)

At a glance

### No access by default

We do not need access to your systems to start. When access helps, you approve the scope and can revoke it at any time.

### Read-only first

Google Analytics and Search Console access, when granted, is normally read-only.

### MFA where supported

Multifactor authentication on company accounts and on client systems that support it.

### No payment data

We never need PCI or payment-card data, and we never move or commit client funds.

Our approach

## How does NativeCode protect client information?

Six principles cover how we handle access, devices and information across SEO, analytics, content, web and growth work.

01

### Limited access

Access to client systems is not required by default. When it is necessary, it is limited to approved systems and the minimum permissions required.

02

### Identity protection

Company accounts use strong passwords and multifactor authentication where supported.

03

### Secure devices

Client work happens on company-managed Apple devices with built-in macOS protections, encryption, screen locking and current updates.

04

### Data minimization

We collect and access only the information needed to perform the agreed services.

05

### Controlled sharing

Client information is not shared with unauthorized third parties or uploaded to external platforms or generative AI tools without authorization.

06

### Confidentiality

Client information is handled as confidential and used only for the purposes of the engagement.

Access, identity and data

## What access does NativeCode need?

Most of our work is strategy, content, analytics and reporting, so most engagements need little or no access to your systems. Where access is granted, these rules apply.

Access

### Client systems

Not required by default. When a client grants access, permissions match the approved scope of work.

Read-only access preferred where available

Individually assigned accounts

MFA enabled where supported

No shared credentials

Access can be revoked by the client at any time

No access to payment-card information

No access to customer records unless expressly required and authorized

Content is normally handed to the client to publish

Publishing access used only when specifically granted

Identity

### Accounts and passwords

Google Workspace manages business identity. Access is assigned by business need and removed when no longer required.

MFA on company accounts

Passwords of at least 12 characters

A unique account for each person

Least-privilege access

Prompt removal of access no longer needed

No routine sharing of passwords

Client-required VPN or trusted-device software installed when an engagement needs it

Data

### Client information

We receive only the analytics, search, content or business information an engagement needs, and only when a client authorizes it.

Search Console access normally read-only

Google Analytics access normally read-only

Data not downloaded or kept unless necessary

Client data is never sold

Not used to train public AI models

Not uploaded to external generative AI platforms without authorization

No PCI or payment-card data required

Client funds are never moved or committed

Device security

## Managed machines, current software.

All client work is done on NativeCode-managed Apple devices used for business.

### Operating systems

Client work runs on supported versions of macOS.

### Built-in protections

XProtect, Gatekeeper, FileVault encryption, System Integrity Protection, the firewall and automatic security updates.

### Device access

Devices are protected by Touch ID or strong device authentication.

### Screen locking

Screens lock automatically after 15 minutes of inactivity or less.

### Software updates

System and app updates are installed promptly. Critical security updates are targeted within seven days, sooner when severity calls for it.

### Business use

Client work is done only on NativeCode-managed devices used for business purposes.

Incident response

## A set process if something goes wrong.

If an incident materially affects client information or systems, the affected client is told promptly, in line with contractual and legal requirements.

01

### Identify

Recognize and log a suspected incident.

02

### Contain

Limit access and stop further exposure.

03

### Investigate

Work out what happened and what it touched.

04

### Remediate

Fix the cause and restore normal operation.

05

### Notify

Tell affected clients promptly.

06

### Review

Record what was learned and update our practices.

Governance

## Written down, and honest about scope.

Our practices are documented and sized to the consulting work we do. We cooperate with client security and procurement reviews.

Documented practices

### Eight areas, all in writing

Information security

Certifications

### Not SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certified

NativeCode is not currently certified under SOC 2 or ISO 27001. Our security practices are designed for the nature and scope of our consulting services, and we will answer reasonable security, procurement and vendor-risk questions as part of your review.

## Common security questions

### Does NativeCode require access to client systems?

No. NativeCode does not require access to client systems by default, and most SEO, content and strategy work can start without it. If access becomes necessary for an engagement, the client must expressly approve it, the scope is limited to what the work needs, and the client can revoke it at any time.

### What type of system access does NativeCode typically use?

Read-only access is preferred whenever possible. For analytics and search-performance platforms such as Google Analytics and Search Console, NativeCode normally asks for read-only access. Edit access is requested only when an engagement requires changes inside a platform, and only with the express approval of the client.

### Does NativeCode access payment-card data?

No. NativeCode does not require access to PCI or payment-card data for its standard services, including SEO, analytics, content, web and growth work. We also never move or commit client funds. Payment systems and card data stay entirely under the control of the client and its payment providers.

### Does NativeCode use multifactor authentication?

Yes. NativeCode uses multifactor authentication on supported company accounts and on client systems that support it. MFA protects the accounts used for analytics, search, content and web work, so a stolen password alone is not enough to sign in. Where a platform does not support MFA, access is kept as limited as possible.

### Is NativeCode SOC 2 certified?

No. NativeCode is not currently SOC 2 certified, and we say so plainly so procurement teams can plan around it. We follow documented security practices covering access, devices, data handling and incident response, and we answer security questionnaires and vendor-risk reviews on request through security@nativecode.ai.

### Is NativeCode ISO 27001 certified?

No. NativeCode is not currently ISO 27001 certified. Our security practices are written down instead, with policies covering information security, access control, passwords and MFA, acceptable use, data handling and incident response. Security teams can request this documentation or send a questionnaire to security@nativecode.ai.

### Does NativeCode upload client information to generative AI systems?

No, not without client authorization. NativeCode does not upload confidential client information to external generative AI systems unless the client has approved it. This covers documents, data exports, analytics and any other material shared during an engagement, and it applies to every engagement we run.

### Can NativeCode comply with client VPN or trusted-device requirements?

Yes, when required and technically appropriate for the engagement. NativeCode can work through client VPNs, on trusted or managed devices, and within other access controls a client security team sets. Share your requirements during scoping so access is set up correctly before any work begins.

### How can a security team request more information?

Email security@nativecode.ai. We respond to reasonable security, procurement and vendor-risk questions, complete security questionnaires and share our written security documentation on request. Include your company name, the engagement in question and any deadline, so we can reply with what your review needs.

FAQ

## AI search optimization questions

### What is AI search optimization?

AI search optimization is the work of making your site easy for AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot and Google AI Overviews to find, understand and cite. It is often called AEO (answer engine optimization) or GEO (generative engine optimization), and it covers crawler access, structured data, entity clarity and answer-ready content.

### Is it different from SEO?

AI search optimization builds on SEO rather than replacing it. Crawlability, structured data and authority still matter. What changes is that AI answers are assembled from individual sections of pages, so content has to be clear, specific and quotable on its own, and your brand has to be described the same way across the web.

### Should we block AI crawlers?

Usually not, and never by accident. Treat search crawlers and training crawlers separately. Blocking search crawlers such as OAI-SearchBot or PerplexityBot keeps you out of those answers. Blocking training crawlers such as GPTBot is a business decision that does not affect Google AI Overviews, so check your robots.txt and CDN rules first.

### How do we measure visibility in AI answers?

Measure it with a mix of traffic data and repeat testing. Track AI referral traffic in GA4, test a fixed set of buyer questions in each assistant every month, log when you are named or cited, and add an AI option to the how did you hear about us field on your forms.

## AI search optimization questions

### What is Answer Engine Optimization?

AEO structures your site and content so AI answer engines like Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity can read, trust and cite it. It covers entity optimization, structured data and answer-formatted content. The goal is to be the source an AI answer quotes, not only a link in a list of results.

### How is AEO different from SEO?

SEO earns rankings in result lists. AEO earns citations inside answers. They share foundations like crawlability, structure and authority, but AEO adds entity clarity, machine-readable trust and quotable formatting. Most sites need both, and we run them as one program.

### How do you measure AI visibility?

We track citations across Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity for a fixed set of prompts, plus entity and schema validation. Those sit alongside rankings, demand captured and revenue, so AI visibility is reported on the same terms as the rest of search.

Questions

## ChatGPT SEO questions

### What is ChatGPT SEO?

ChatGPT SEO is the practice of making a brand easy for ChatGPT search to find, understand and cite. It combines crawler access, consistent entity facts, answer-first content, structured data and mentions on trusted third-party sites. The same work usually helps in Perplexity and Google AI Overviews, because these engines read the web in similar ways.

### How does ChatGPT search find sources?

ChatGPT search sends queries to third-party search providers, including Microsoft Bing, and uses OpenAI's OAI-SearchBot crawler to read pages. It then summarizes what it finds and links the sources it relied on. Pages blocked in robots.txt, missing from Bing's index or hard to render are less likely to be read or cited.

### How do you optimize for Perplexity as well?

Perplexity works in a similar way: it runs a live search, reads sources with its PerplexityBot crawler and cites them inline. We allow PerplexityBot in robots.txt, keep key facts in plain text near the top of each page, and pursue mentions on sources Perplexity already cites for your topics. Both engines are tracked with the same prompt set.

### Can you guarantee ChatGPT will cite my brand?

No. Nobody can guarantee a citation in ChatGPT or Perplexity. Answers change with the prompt, the user's location, model updates and whatever the live search returns that day. What we can control is whether your pages are crawlable, clear, consistent and worth citing, and we measure progress on a fixed prompt set instead of promising placements.

### How do you measure ChatGPT visibility?

We run a fixed set of real buyer prompts in ChatGPT and Perplexity on a set schedule and log whether your brand is mentioned, cited or missing, and who appears instead. We pair that with referral traffic from chatgpt.com and perplexity.ai in GA4. Using the same prompts every time keeps the results comparable.

Schema audit

## What does a schema markup audit check?

A schema markup audit checks these five things in order, because valid markup only helps when it is also accurate.

1. Is the markup valid? JSON-LD syntax, required and recommended properties, and errors in the Rich Results Test.
2. Does it match the page? Prices, availability, ratings and FAQ text must match what visitors see.
3. Are entities connected? One Organization @id, sameAs links to real profiles, and the same name, address and phone everywhere.
4. Is it eligible? Which rich results Google still shows for your types, and which no longer apply.
5. Does it hold after releases? Search Console enhancement reports and spot checks after theme or CMS changes.

FAQ

## Questions about schema markup

### What is schema markup?

Schema markup is structured data, usually written as JSON-LD, that describes a page using the Schema.org vocabulary shared by the major search engines. It tells Google, Bing and AI answer engines exactly what a page is about, such as a product with a price, a service, an article or a business with an address, instead of leaving them to infer it from the text.

### Does schema markup improve rankings?

Schema markup is not a direct ranking factor, according to Google. It helps search engines understand your pages and can make them eligible for rich results such as product prices, review stars and breadcrumbs, which change how your listing looks in search. Eligibility does not guarantee a rich result: Google decides when to show one.

### Which schema types should my site use?

Most sites need Organization or LocalBusiness, BreadcrumbList on inner pages, and one type per template: Product and Offer for product pages, Service for service pages and Article for posts. FAQPage fits pages with a visible FAQ. Review and AggregateRating belong only on pages that show genuine reviews and follow Google's review snippet guidelines.

### How do you add schema markup on Shopify, Webflow or WordPress?

We add JSON-LD to templates rather than page by page. On Shopify that means Liquid theme sections that pull product, price and availability data. On Webflow we use page and CMS template custom code bound to CMS fields. On WordPress we configure an SEO plugin or write theme code. Every template is validated before release.

### Does structured data help with AI search?

Yes, structured data helps AI answer engines read your entity facts consistently: your business name, services, products and locations. Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity still decide what to cite on their own, so schema works alongside clear, crawlable content and consistent facts across the web. We treat it as one input, not a guarantee of citations.

Questions

## SEO architecture questions

### Is this SEO or something broader?

Both. Structure, entities and schema decide how Google and AI answer engines read a site, so we design for them as one system rather than chasing rankings page by page. The same architecture supports navigation, analytics and content planning, not only search.

### How do you work with product and engineering?

We join planning, write specs your engineers can build from and check each release before it ships. Decisions made upstream then do not create SEO problems downstream. Specs include URL rules, template requirements, schema and acceptance checks your team can test against.

### Do you only advise, or do you implement?

Both. Engagements range from an audit and roadmap to a full implementation build or an enterprise migration, as a one-off project or a monthly governance retainer. Many teams start with the blueprint and bring us in to implement the parts their engineers cannot schedule.

### Do you cover AI search visibility?

Yes. We look at how large language models and answer engines interpret your content, entities and structure. Then we build the structured data and page formats that make citation more likely, and track how Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity describe the site.

### How do you measure success?

We measure crawl efficiency, indexation health, ranking coverage, demand captured and revenue from organic search. Every recommendation is tied to one of them, so you can see which structural changes paid off and which areas of the site still need work next quarter.

## Topic clusters questions

### What exactly is a topic cluster?

A topic cluster is a pillar page and the articles that support it. One pillar page plus its supporting articles, fully interlinked, roughly 15,000 engineered words per cluster. Every page ships with JSON-LD schema, entity optimization and answer blocks, published to your site and validated.

### Is this content writing or something more?

More. We deliver engineered clusters, not raw word counts. Every cluster is built to rank in Google and get cited in AI answers, so research, structure, schema, internal links and publishing are part of the work. Writing is one step in that process, not the whole service.

### How does the process work?

You pick a volume and share the queries you want to own. We map the entities, gaps and search intent behind each one, then write, mark up, link and publish the full cluster. You review drafts before they go live, and we validate every page after publishing.

### Do clusters target AI answer engines?

Yes. Every cluster targets citation in AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity alongside Google rankings. The method holds a verified unbranded AI Overview citation on a DA 34 domain. Answer blocks, clear definitions and consistent entities make each page easier for those tools to quote.

### How do you measure success?

We measure rankings, AI citations and demand captured. Larger programs include AI Overview citation tracking and quarterly reviews tied to revenue. Each cluster is reported as a unit, so you can see how the pillar and its supporting pages perform together.

Content that gets cited

## How do you write content that AI answers cite?

AI answer engines quote content that is easy to extract and trust. We write to these rules.

1. Answer the question in the first one or two sentences.
2. Use headings phrased the way people ask.
3. Put steps in numbered lists and comparisons in tables.
4. Name concrete things: platforms, places and standards.
5. Keep facts consistent with the rest of the site and add schema.

FAQ

## Questions about content marketing

### What does a content marketing agency do?

A content marketing agency plans, writes and publishes content that brings the right audience to your site and moves them toward buying. For us that means SEO content built around buyer questions, structured to rank in Google and to be cited in AI answers.

### Who writes the content?

Our writers and editors produce briefs and drafts, and your subject experts review them for accuracy before anything is published. For technical topics we interview your team first, so each piece reflects real expertise and first-hand detail rather than a summary of articles that already rank.

### How is this different from topic clusters?

Topic clusters are one part of content marketing: a pillar page and linked supporting articles on one subject. Content marketing also covers research, the editorial calendar, writing, refreshes of older posts and measurement across all your topics. Our topic clusters page explains that method in detail.

### How long until content ranks?

New articles often start ranking within a few months, depending on your site's authority and the competition for each topic. Clusters build faster than single posts because the linked articles support each other. We track rankings, AI citations and leads by article every month.

### Do you use AI to write content?

We use AI tools for research and first-draft support, but every piece is planned, edited and fact-checked by people. Content that only repeats what is already online rarely ranks or gets cited, so each article needs original detail from your team and a clear point of view.

FAQ

## Digital PR questions

### What is digital PR?

Digital PR is the practice of earning online coverage for a brand through stories that publications want to run. It uses data studies, expert commentary and useful tools as the source of the story. Each piece of coverage can bring a link, a brand mention and referral traffic, which supports search rankings and AI search visibility.

### Is digital PR the same as link building?

Not exactly. Digital PR is one way to build links: it earns them through editorial coverage instead of asking site owners for links one at a time. It also earns brand mentions without links and reaches new audiences. Most link building programs combine digital PR with resource outreach and linkable assets.

### Do you buy links or use PBNs?

No. We do not buy links, use private blog networks (PBNs), swap links or pass off sponsored posts as editorial coverage. Those tactics break Google's spam policies and can lead to links being ignored or to manual actions. Every placement we report was earned because a writer chose to cover the story or cite the source.

### How does digital PR help with AI search?

Digital PR gives AI answer engines more credible third-party sources to draw on. ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews often describe brands using news, trade and review sites rather than the brand's own pages. Coverage and mentions on those sites help these engines describe what you do, alongside the links that support classic rankings.

### How do you report on digital PR results?

Every report lists each placement with the publication, the article URL, whether it links to you, the page it points to and the date it went live. We also track brand mentions, referral traffic in GA4 and ranking changes on the pages that gained links, so coverage can be tied to search results.

### What is enterprise SEO?

# International SEO agency for brands going global.

An international SEO agency sets up your site so the right page ranks in each country and language. NativeCode is an Atlanta-based international SEO agency that handles hreflang, market structure, localized keyword research and AI search tracking for brands entering new markets, working with clients across the US.

[Start a project](https://www.nativecode.ai/company/contact) [National SEO](https://www.nativecode.ai/services/national-seo)

Where it goes wrong

## Why does the wrong page show up in the wrong country?

The wrong page shows up because search engines cannot tell which version is for whom. Most international problems come from structure, not content, so markets end up competing with each other.

01

### Missing or broken hreflang

Without correct hreflang, UK shoppers see US prices and Spanish speakers land on English pages.

02

### Translated, not localized

Direct translation misses the words people actually search in each market, so pages exist but do not rank.

03

### One domain, no local trust

A new market starts with few local links or mentions, so even good pages struggle to rank.

FAQ

## International SEO questions

### Should we use subfolders or country domains?

Subfolders suit most brands. Folders such as /uk/ or /es/ keep all authority on one domain and are easier to manage. Country domains can build more local trust but need their own links and upkeep. We recommend a structure based on your markets, your team and how much each market will be maintained.

### What is hreflang?

Hreflang is a tag that tells search engines which language and country each version of a page is for, so they show the right one to each searcher. It has to be set on every version and point both ways to work. Missing or one-way tags are one of the most common international SEO errors.

### Is translating our site enough?

No. People in each market use their own terms, and some products need different names, prices or proof. Localized pages built on local keyword research rank far better than direct translations. We map demand in each language first, then plan the pages each market actually needs.

### Do you translate the content?

No, we plan it and review it. We set the content, keywords and structure for each market and work with your translators or native-speaking partners on the final language. Then we review every page for search before launch, including titles, headings, hreflang and internal links.

Questions

## Link building services questions

### Do you buy links?

No. We do not use paid link networks, PBNs or link exchanges. Those links can be discounted or penalized by Google, and they rarely come from sites your buyers read. Every link we report was earned through outreach, digital PR or an asset that another site chose to cite.

### Where do the links come from?

The links come from news sites, trade publications and niche blogs that cover your category. We earn them through outreach and digital PR, usually built around original data, expert commentary or a useful tool. Relevance to your market matters more to us than raw domain metrics.

### Do links help with AI search?

Yes. AI answer engines lean on sources that other trusted sites cite, so earned coverage supports both rankings and citations. A brand that is mentioned and linked by credible publications is easier for Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity to describe accurately.

### How do you report results?

Every placement is listed with the linking URL, the page it points to and the date it went live. Reports also show which target pages gained links and how their rankings moved, so you can connect the coverage to search results instead of counting links on their own.

### Can tools and calculators earn links?

Yes. People link to calculators and tools because they use them, and a good tool keeps earning links long after launch. We build those too, through our interactive tools work, and run outreach to the sites and writers who cover the problem the tool solves.

FAQ

## Local SEO services questions

### What is local AEO?

Local AEO is answer engine optimization for local questions. It means making your business facts, services, areas and reviews clear and consistent so AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Mode can recommend you when someone asks for a business nearby. It builds on the same profile, page and review work as local SEO.

### How long does local SEO take?

Local SEO usually shows early movement within weeks and builds over several months. Profile, category and citation fixes can move map rankings quickly. Location pages, reviews and local links take longer to compound. We report progress monthly, by location and search term, so you can see what is moving and what comes next.

### Do I need an office in each town to rank there?

No, but distance matters for map results. Google weighs the distance from the searcher to your verified address, so map rankings are strongest near your location. Service area businesses can still rank in nearby towns with strong relevance and reviews, and a useful page for each area helps in regular results.

### Do you work with multi-location brands?

Yes. We manage Google Business Profiles, location pages and reviews across many locations from one plan, with reporting by location so you can compare markets side by side. Franchises, chains and clinics with several branches usually start with a data cleanup across every profile before new pages are built.

The search problem

## Why does every location need its own SEO plan?

Every location needs its own plan because each one is its own search market. Map results depend on distance from the searcher, so a branch only ranks well near its own address, with its own profile, page and reviews.

01

### Profiles drift

Hours, categories and phone numbers change one location at a time, and the errors spread to maps and directories.

02

### Copied location pages

Pages that only swap the city name rarely rank and can be treated as doorway pages.

03

### No view across locations

Without reporting by location, it is hard to see which ones lead and which are falling behind.

FAQ

## Multi-location SEO questions

### Does every location need its own page?

Yes, if it has its own address. Each location page should be linked from a crawlable store locator, link to its Google Business Profile and carry details that are unique to that location, such as hours, team, services offered there and nearby landmarks. Thin copies of one template rarely rank.

### How do we avoid duplicate location pages?

Use one template for structure, then add what only that location has. That means its team, the services offered there, nearby landmarks, local reviews and real photos. Pages that differ only by city name can be treated as duplicates, so the unique details are what make each page worth indexing.

### Can franchisees manage their own profiles?

They can, but brand-level control of the core data prevents errors. We usually keep the brand as the owner of every Google Business Profile and give each location manager access to posts, photos and review replies. That keeps names, categories and hours consistent while local teams stay involved.

### How do you report across many locations?

Each location is tracked for calls, direction requests, leads and map rankings, then ranked side by side. You can see which locations lead, which need work and why. Reports roll up to the brand level each month, with notes on what changed and what we will do next.

National versus local

## How is national SEO different from local SEO?

National SEO is won on authority, not distance. Local rankings lean on your address and your map listing. National rankings depend on how well your site covers a topic and how much the rest of the web trusts it.

01

### No map to lean on

There is no map pack for national searches. Every result is earned by the page itself and the site behind it.

02

### Bigger competitors

You compete with national brands, marketplaces and review sites that have years of links and content.

03

### More pages to get right

National sites have more categories, products and topics, so structure and crawl control matter far more.

FAQ

## National SEO questions

### What is the difference between local and national SEO?

Local SEO targets searches near a location, and national SEO targets searches across the whole country. Local SEO works mostly through Google Maps, location pages and reviews. National SEO depends on site structure, content depth and links rather than distance, because there is no map pack to lean on.

### How long does national SEO take?

National SEO usually takes six to twelve months to compound in competitive markets. Technical fixes can show results within weeks, because they help pages that already exist. Content and authority take longer to build. We report monthly by page group so you can see which parts of the site are moving.

### Do you work with companies outside Atlanta?

Yes. NativeCode is based in Atlanta and works with clients across the US, mostly remotely. National programs run on shared dashboards, monthly reporting and regular calls with your marketing, product and engineering teams, so location is rarely a factor in how the work gets done.

### Can you run national and local SEO together?

Yes. Multi-location brands often need both: national pages for category and product searches, and location pages and profiles for each branch. We plan them as one program so the national pages and the local pages support each other instead of competing for the same searches.

FAQ

## Questions about SEO services

### How long does SEO take to work?

Most sites see technical fixes picked up within weeks of release, while content and authority work builds over several months. The timeline depends on your starting point, your competition and how quickly changes ship. We report monthly so you can see what is moving and what is next.

### What is the difference between SEO and AEO?

SEO earns rankings in classic search results. AEO, or answer engine optimization, earns mentions and citations in AI answers such as Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity. Both depend on clear structure, schema and trusted content, so we run them as one program rather than two.

### Do you work with in-house teams and developers?

Yes. We work alongside in-house marketing, content and engineering teams every week. We can implement changes ourselves on Shopify, Webflow and WordPress, or write clear specs and tickets your developers can build from. Before each release we check the work on staging so nothing ships that could hurt rankings.

### How do you report on SEO results?

We report monthly on the numbers that matter to the business: organic leads and revenue, traffic to key pages, rankings for target searches and AI answer visibility. Reports come from GA4 and Search Console, with a short list of what we will do next.

### Are you an Atlanta SEO company or a national agency?

Both. NativeCode is based in the Atlanta metro area, with an office in Norcross, and serves clients across the United States. Most engagements run remotely with scheduled calls and shared reporting. Atlanta clients can also meet in person. Local businesses can start with our local SEO service.

FAQ

## Questions about SEO audits

### Is the SEO audit really free?

Yes. You get the findings and the priority list whether or not you hire us. We offer the free audit because it is the fastest way for both sides to see whether there is a fit, and because a clear list of fixes is useful to your team either way.

### What do I get from the audit?

You get a written list of the issues holding your rankings back, the pages they affect, the fix for each and an order to do them in, ranked by revenue impact. It covers technical SEO, content, links and AI search visibility.

### How long does the free audit take?

A senior strategist reviews your site by hand, so timing depends on its size and complexity. We confirm when to expect the findings once we receive your request, and we email them as soon as the review is done. A full paid audit for a large or enterprise site is scoped separately.

### What is the difference between the app and the audit?

The NativeCode Audit app at app.nativecode.ai runs an automated check of key technical and AI visibility signals that you can repeat any time. The free audit on this page is a manual review by a senior strategist who explains causes and priorities, which an automated tool cannot do.

### Do you need access to our analytics?

No, not for the free audit. We can review a lot from outside the site, including crawlability, structure, content and AI answers. If you share read access to Search Console and GA4, the findings get more specific, and we treat that data as confidential.

## Questions about SEO consulting

### What does an SEO consultant do?

An SEO consultant diagnoses what is limiting organic growth, sets priorities and guides the people who do the work. That includes audits, roadmaps, migration plans, developer specs and release checks. The consultant does not replace your team; they make its search decisions faster and safer.

### Is a consultant better than an SEO agency?

Neither is better in general. A consultant suits teams that already have writers and developers and need senior direction. An agency suits teams that also need the work implemented. We offer both, and many clients start with consulting before adding implementation.

### Who will we work with?

You work directly with a senior strategist, not an account manager. The same person runs the audit, writes the roadmap, joins your calls and reviews the work your team ships. There are no junior handoffs between the sale and the work.

### Can you help with a site migration?

Yes. Migrations are one of the most common consulting projects we take on. We map every URL, plan redirects, review the staging site, check launch day and monitor Search Console afterward. The goal is for rankings and traffic to carry over to the new platform without a long recovery period.

### Do you consult on AI search?

Yes. We advise teams on how to get cited in Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity. That covers entity clarity, schema, answer-first content and consistent facts about your organization across your site and the wider web. We also show where AI answers currently name competitors instead of you, and why.

Services · Shopify architecture

# Shopify SEO for stores at catalog scale.

Shopify SEO is the work that helps a Shopify store rank its collections and products in Google and appear in AI shopping answers. NativeCode is an Atlanta-based team that runs Shopify SEO for ecommerce brands nationwide, from collection taxonomy and faceted navigation to product schema across thousands of SKUs.

[Start a project](https://www.nativecode.ai/company/contact) [See CRO](https://www.nativecode.ai/services/conversion-rate-optimization)

What’s included

## Why does Shopify SEO fail at the structure layer?

Shopify SEO usually fails at the structure layer, not the plugin layer. Duplicate collections, crawl traps and thin product pages hold stores back, so we design the taxonomy and data systems that prevent them.

01

### Collection taxonomy

Logical collection hierarchies and clean URL structures that capture demand at every level of the catalog.

02

### Faceted navigation

Filters that help shoppers without creating thousands of crawlable duplicate URLs.

03

### Product schema

Product, Offer, Review and Breadcrumb markup across every SKU, for rich results and AI shopping answers.

04

### Programmatic SEO

Template systems that turn your catalog into search-ready pages, built once and compounding with every product.

05

### Indexation and internal links

URL governance, canonicals and linking that send authority to the collections and products that sell.

06

### Restructures and migrations

Fix an existing store in place, or replatform, with full redirect mapping so rankings carry over.

## Shopify SEO questions

### What does Shopify architecture include?

Shopify architecture includes collection taxonomy, URL governance, faceted navigation strategy, product schema, internal linking and indexation control. It is the structural layer that decides how search engines read your catalog, which collections rank and which filter pages stay out of the index.

### Can you fix an existing store without replatforming?

Yes. We restructure collections, navigation and schema in place, keep what already ranks and map redirects wherever URLs change. Most stores do not need a new platform to fix search problems. They need a clear plan for which pages exist and why.

### Do you handle product schema?

Yes. We set up full structured data across every SKU, including Product, Offer, Review and Breadcrumb graphs. That qualifies your catalog for rich results and helps AI shopping answers read prices, availability and reviews correctly. Markup always matches what the page shows.

### Does this work with AI answer engines?

Yes. Entity and schema systems make your products easier to cite in Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity shopping answers. Accurate product facts, consistent naming and clear buying guides give those tools reliable sources to quote when shoppers ask what to buy.

### How do you measure success?

We measure organic revenue, indexation health, ranking coverage across the catalog and AI citations. These are commerce metrics, not traffic for its own sake. Reports break results down by collection, so you can see which parts of the catalog are growing.

Field data vs lab data

## How does Google measure site speed?

Google measures site speed with field data from real Chrome users in the Chrome UX Report (CrUX), and assesses Core Web Vitals at the 75th percentile of page visits.

1. Largest Contentful Paint (LCP): how long the main image or text block takes to appear.
2. Interaction to Next Paint (INP): how quickly the page responds to taps, clicks and key presses.
3. Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS): how much the layout jumps while the page loads.
4. Field data: real-user CrUX results shown in Search Console and PageSpeed Insights over a rolling 28-day window.
5. Lab data: Lighthouse tests run in a controlled setting, useful for debugging but not what Google uses to assess Core Web Vitals.

FAQ

## Questions about site speed optimization

### What is site speed optimization?

Site speed optimization is the work of making web pages load faster, respond sooner and stay visually stable for real visitors. It covers images, fonts, JavaScript, third-party scripts, theme code, caching and CDN setup. The goal is to pass Google's Core Web Vitals in field data and give visitors a faster experience, especially on mobile.

### Why is my PageSpeed Insights score different from Search Console?

They often show different data. The PageSpeed Insights performance score comes from a single Lighthouse lab test on a simulated device. The Search Console Core Web Vitals report uses field data from real Chrome users over a rolling 28-day window. Google assesses Core Web Vitals on field data, so we use lab tests to debug and field data to judge progress.

### Do Shopify apps slow down a store?

They can. Many Shopify apps add their own JavaScript, CSS and network requests to every page, even pages where the app is not used, and code from uninstalled apps can stay in the theme. We review each app and tag, remove what is unused, load the rest only where it is needed, and consolidate tracking in one tag manager setup.

### Does site speed affect conversions?

Speed can affect conversions, but the size of the effect differs by site, so we do not promise a set lift. Slow product pages, laggy filters and layout shifts during checkout add friction for buyers. We compare conversion rate by template in GA4 before and after speed releases, and pair speed work with conversion rate optimization when testing is needed.

### How long does site speed optimization take?

The first round of fixes usually takes a few weeks, depending on the platform, the number of templates and how many apps and scripts are involved. Lab results change as soon as a fix is released. Field data in CrUX and Search Console updates over a rolling 28-day window, so confirmed Core Web Vitals changes take about a month to show.

Technical SEO audit

## What does a technical SEO audit check?

A technical SEO audit checks these areas in order, because each one depends on the one before.

1. Can search engines crawl the site? Robots rules, server responses and internal links.
2. Are the right pages indexed? Canonicals, noindex rules, sitemaps and duplicates.
3. Do pages render and load fast? JavaScript rendering, Core Web Vitals and mobile layout.
4. Is the structure clear? URLs, navigation, breadcrumbs and internal linking depth.
5. Is the content understood? Titles, headings, schema and entity signals for AI search.

FAQ

## Questions about technical SEO

### What is technical SEO?

Technical SEO is the work that lets search engines and AI crawlers find, render and understand a website. It covers crawling, indexation, site speed, structured data, site architecture and redirects. Content and links only pay off when this foundation is working.

### How is technical SEO different from on-page SEO?

Technical SEO deals with how the whole site is built and served, such as crawl rules, speed and schema. On-page SEO deals with what each page says, such as titles, headings and copy. Most sites need both, and we handle them together.

### Do you implement fixes or only recommend them?

Both. We implement fixes directly on Shopify, Webflow and WordPress, and write developer-ready specs for custom stacks and headless builds. After each release we check Search Console and recrawl the affected pages to confirm the fix worked, then move to the next item on the list.

### How long does a technical SEO audit take?

A technical SEO audit usually takes a few weeks. The timing depends on site size and on how many templates, platforms and markets are involved, so large ecommerce and enterprise sites take longer. You get findings ranked by impact with the pages each issue affects, not a raw export from a crawler.

### Does technical SEO help with AI search?

Yes. AI answer engines rely on crawlable pages, clear structure and structured data to understand what a business does. Clean schema, consistent entity facts and fast, renderable pages make it easier for Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity to cite you.

FAQ

## Questions about WordPress SEO

### Is WordPress good for SEO?

Yes. WordPress can rank very well when the theme is fast, plugins are kept lean and the site structure is planned. Most WordPress SEO problems come from plugin bloat, duplicate archive pages and heavy page builders, which can all be fixed.

### Which SEO plugin should we use?

Yoast and Rank Math both work well. What matters is using one, configuring it correctly and making sure your theme does not output its own titles or schema at the same time. We review and fix the setup you have.

### Should we move from WordPress to Webflow or Shopify?

Only if WordPress no longer suits how your team works or what the site must do. Many sites are better served by fixing WordPress than by migrating. If a move makes sense, such as Shopify for a growing store, we plan it with full redirects so rankings carry over.

### Do you work on WooCommerce?

Yes. We work on WooCommerce stores to improve speed, product schema, category structure and faceted navigation. When a store has outgrown WooCommerce, we can also migrate it to Shopify with every product and category URL redirected, so the store keeps its search traffic.

### Can you build new WordPress pages and templates?

Yes. We build custom Gutenberg blocks, templates and integrations in WordPress, so your team can publish new pages without a heavy page builder slowing the site. Each template is built with clean headings, schema and fast loading, so new pages start on a strong SEO footing.

# BigCommerce to Shopify migration with every URL mapped.

NativeCode handles BigCommerce to Shopify migration, moving products, options, custom fields, customers, orders and content, with a 301 redirect for every changed URL. A BigCommerce to Shopify migration includes products, options, custom fields, customers, orders, reviews, content, redirects and integrations, restructured for Shopify.

01

BigCommerce variant options become Shopify variants. Shopify allows three options per product, so larger option sets are split or handled with metafields or an options app.

02

Modifiers such as text fields, checkboxes and file uploads move to line item properties or a product options app. Custom fields become metafields.

Every BigCommerce product, category, brand, page and blog URL mapped to its Shopify URL, including your existing 301 rules.

ERP, inventory and supplier EDI connections moved to Shopify and tested before go-live so orders keep moving.

[EDI and ecommerce operations →](https://www.nativecode.ai/services/edi-integration)

06

### Customers, orders and reviews

Customers, addresses, order history and product reviews imported. Passwords cannot move, so customers are invited to reactivate their accounts.

How we run it

## How do you migrate BigCommerce to Shopify?

We migrate BigCommerce to Shopify in five steps, with data tested on a staging store before any DNS change.

1. Step 1

    ### Audit

    Export products, customers and orders, crawl every URL and list apps, options, modifiers and custom fields.

2. Step 2

    Decide how each option set and modifier fits Shopify variants, and map old URLs to new ones.

    Build the Shopify theme, set up apps and metafields, and import data to a staging store.

4. Step 4

    ### Launch

5. Step 5

    ### Monitor

    Watch Search Console, orders and ERP or EDI feeds, and fix gaps as they appear.

What we moveProducts and variantsCustom fieldsCustomersOrder historyReviewsPages and blog posts301 redirects

URLs and redirects

## How do BigCommerce URLs map to Shopify?

BigCommerce URLs map to Shopify's fixed /products/, /collections/, /pages/ and /blogs/ paths, so most URLs change and each needs a 301 redirect. BigCommerce can serve products and categories from the root of the domain; Shopify cannot.

### Product pages

/blue-jacket/ becomes /products/blue-jacket. Older stores that still use .html product URLs are mapped the same way.

### Category and brand pages

/jackets/ becomes /collections/jackets. Brand pages become collections built from the Shopify vendor field.

### Web pages and blog posts

/shipping-returns/ becomes /pages/shipping-returns, and /blog/post-name/ becomes /blogs/news/post-name.

[All Shopify migrations →](https://www.nativecode.ai/services/shopify-migration)

### Filter and search URLs

Filtered category and search URLs redirect to the parent collection, not one by one. Shopify Search & Discovery handles the new filters.

FAQ

## Questions about BigCommerce to Shopify migration

### Will we lose SEO rankings moving from BigCommerce to Shopify?

Not if the migration is planned for search. Because Shopify adds /products/ and /collections/ to URLs, nearly every BigCommerce product and category URL changes. We map each one with a 301 redirect, carry over titles, meta descriptions and content, and monitor Search Console after launch to fix any gaps quickly.

### How do BigCommerce options and modifiers move to Shopify?

Variant options move to Shopify variants, and modifiers move to line item properties or a product options app. Shopify allows three options per product, so products with more option types are restructured, split into separate products or handled with an options app. We agree the approach for each product type before importing anything.

### What happens to BigCommerce custom fields?

Custom fields become Shopify metafields. We create a metafield definition for each field you use, import the values and show them on product pages through the theme. Fields that shoppers filter by can also power collection filters in Shopify Search & Discovery, so specs stay useful after the move.

### Can you migrate BigCommerce B2B Edition to Shopify?

Yes, usually to Shopify Plus B2B. Company accounts, buyers, customer group pricing and payment terms map to Shopify companies, catalogs and payment terms. Features such as shopping lists, quote workflows or a custom buyer portal may need an app or custom work, so we list each B2B Edition feature you use and plan its replacement first.

### Can customers keep their accounts and order history?

Customer records, addresses and order history can move from BigCommerce to Shopify, but passwords cannot be migrated for security reasons. After launch, customers receive an account invitation so they can set a new password. We import historical orders for reference and reporting and check totals on a staging store first.

Questions

## CRM integration questions

### Which CRMs do you integrate with?

We work mainly with HubSpot and Salesforce, and with other CRMs that have a documented API. We connect them to website forms, Shopify and other ecommerce platforms, Google Ads, Meta, LinkedIn and email platforms such as Klaviyo. Native integrations come first, with middleware or custom code only where they fall short.

### How do you pass UTM data and click IDs into the CRM?

We capture UTM parameters, click IDs such as GCLID and FBCLID, the landing page and the referrer when a visitor arrives, store them in first-party cookies and write them into hidden form fields. When the form is submitted, the CRM saves them on the contact and the deal. Reports can then show which campaign produced each lead, opportunity and closed deal.

### What are offline conversion imports?

Offline conversion imports send results that happen after the form fill, such as a qualified lead or a closed deal, back to the ad platforms. Google Ads matches them by click ID or enhanced conversions data, and Meta receives them through the Conversions API. Bidding can then optimize toward leads that turn into revenue instead of every form submission.

### Can you sync Shopify customers and orders to HubSpot or Salesforce?

Yes. We sync Shopify customers, orders and products to HubSpot with its Shopify integration or to Salesforce with a connector or middleware, then map fields and lifecycle stages. Sales and service teams see order history on each record, and marketing can segment by purchase behavior. We test duplicates and edge cases such as guest checkouts before switching it on.

### How do you keep CRM data clean?

We keep CRM data clean with rules at the point of entry and regular checks. That means required fields, standard values for sources and stages, deduplication by email and company domain, and naming rules for properties. We also audit the CRM every month for duplicates, empty fields and broken integrations, and fix issues before they reach reports.

# Dropship automation for supplier inventory and orders.

Dropship automation connects your store to dropship and wholesale suppliers, so stock levels, prices, orders and tracking numbers move on their own instead of by spreadsheet and email. NativeCode is an Atlanta-based team that builds these supplier connections for Shopify and other stores nationwide, using supplier APIs, SFTP and CSV feeds or EDI.

[Start a project](https://www.nativecode.ai/company/contact) [See the ThirdLust build](https://www.nativecode.ai/thirdlust-case-study)

What’s included

## What does dropship automation include?

Dropship automation includes supplier connections, inventory and price sync, order routing, tracking updates, backorder handling and monitoring. Each supplier connects through whatever it supports: an API, an SFTP or CSV feed, or EDI.

01

### Supplier connections

Each dropship or wholesale supplier connects by API, SFTP and CSV feed or X12 EDI, all feeding one flow into your store.

02

### Inventory and price sync

Stock and cost updates run on a schedule set for each supplier, so listings and margins stay current.

03

### Automatic order routing

Each order is split by line and sent to the supplier that holds the stock, by rules your team controls.

04

### Tracking back to the store

Ship notices and tracking numbers flow back to Shopify, which marks orders fulfilled and notifies the customer.

05

### Backorders and discontinued items

Backordered and discontinued items are hidden, flagged or rerouted to another supplier before they sell.

06

### Monitoring and alerts

Stale feeds, rejected orders and missing tracking trigger alerts to a named owner before a customer notices.

How we run it

## How do you automate dropship orders across multiple suppliers?

You automate dropship orders across multiple suppliers by mapping every supplier SKU to your catalog, syncing stock on a schedule and routing each order line by rules. We run it in four steps, one supplier at a time.

This is the kind of supplier work behind the [Spooky Costumes](https://www.nativecode.ai/spooky-costumes-case-study) and [ThirdLust](https://www.nativecode.ai/thirdlust-case-study) builds, which connected each store to its suppliers with EDI.

01

### Map suppliers and SKUs

List each supplier, its feed format and schedule, and map supplier SKUs, UPCs and attributes to your catalog.

02

### Connect and sync

Build the API, SFTP, CSV or EDI connection for each supplier and set sync schedules for stock and price.

03

### Route and test

Set routing rules, then run test orders end to end until tracking returns to the store.

04

### Run and monitor

Go live supplier by supplier, with alerts for stale feeds, failed orders and missing tracking.

Questions

## Dropship automation questions

### What is dropship automation?

Dropship automation is the set of integrations that move inventory, orders and tracking between your store and the suppliers who ship for you. Supplier stock syncs into the store, each order goes to the right supplier without manual entry, and tracking comes back to the customer. It replaces spreadsheets, emailed orders and copy-pasted tracking numbers.

### How often should supplier inventory sync?

Inventory should sync as often as the supplier can provide reliable data, and fast-moving items need it most. Supplier APIs can usually be checked often, while SFTP and CSV feeds update on the supplier's own schedule. We set a schedule per supplier and can hold back a buffer on low-stock items so the store does not oversell between updates.

### How do you handle products sold by more than one supplier?

Products sold by more than one supplier are mapped to a single listing, with each supplier's SKU, cost and stock attached. Routing rules then pick the supplier for each order, for example by stock on hand, cost or ship-from location. Customers see one product, and your team sees which supplier filled each order.

### What happens with backorders and discontinued items?

Backordered and discontinued items are handled by rules you approve. When a supplier marks an item backordered, the store can hide it, show an expected date or route the order to another supplier. Discontinued items are unpublished or redirected so customers and search engines are not sent to dead pages, and every change is logged for your team.

### Do I need EDI for dropship automation?

No. Most dropship automation runs on supplier APIs or SFTP and CSV feeds. EDI is needed when a supplier or retail partner requires it, which some larger suppliers do. We connect whatever each supplier supports and bring every supplier into one flow, and our X12 EDI integration service covers the partners that require standard documents.

FAQ

## Questions about ecommerce web design

### How long does an ecommerce website build take?

An ecommerce build usually takes a few months. The timing depends on catalog size, integrations and whether products, customers and orders are being migrated from another platform. Larger catalogs and custom features take longer. You get a written timeline before work starts and progress reviews at each stage.

### Should we use Shopify or a custom build?

Most brands are best served by Shopify, because checkout, payments and apps are reliable and well supported. A custom build makes sense when the catalog, pricing or buying flow needs something no theme or app can do. We recommend after the review.

### Can you redesign our store without losing rankings?

Yes. We map every product, collection and content URL, carry over titles, descriptions and schema, and set 301 redirects before launch. After go-live we monitor Search Console for crawl errors and ranking changes and fix any gaps quickly, so the redesign keeps the search traffic you already earned.

### Do you connect suppliers and inventory?

Yes. We have built supplier EDI connections for inventory and order routing for ecommerce brands. Connecting operations during the build means stock levels, purchase orders and shipping confirmations move automatically from day one, with fewer manual errors reaching customers after launch.

### Do you have ecommerce case studies?

Yes. Our case studies include search architecture for a large-catalog online retailer, HauteFlair, and product page changes that raised its conversion rate. We also built supplier EDI connections for ecommerce brands. You can read each case study on our site and see the Proof section on this page.

# EDI integration that connects your store and suppliers.

EDI integration connects your online store to the suppliers who hold your stock, so inventory, orders, tracking and invoices move without manual entry. NativeCode is an Atlanta-based team that builds and monitors EDI connections for Shopify retailers nationwide, the same work behind our Spooky Costumes case study.

[Start a project](https://www.nativecode.ai/company/contact) [See the Spooky Costumes build](https://www.nativecode.ai/spooky-costumes-case-study)

What’s included

## What does EDI integration include?

EDI integration includes inventory sync, purchase orders and routing, acknowledgments and shipping, invoices, catalog onboarding and monitoring. Large catalogs and dropship models break when stock, orders and tracking move by spreadsheet and email, so we replace that with automated document flows.

Trading with retailers on X12 standards? See [X12 EDI integration](https://www.nativecode.ai/services/x12-edi). Syncing stock and orders with dropship suppliers? See [dropship automation](https://www.nativecode.ai/services/dropship-automation).

01

### Inventory sync

Supplier stock levels flow into the store on a schedule, so products only sell when someone can ship them.

02

### Purchase orders and routing

Each order is split by supplier and sent as a purchase order to the one that holds the stock.

03

### Acknowledgments and shipping

Order confirmations, ship notices and tracking numbers come back automatically and update the customer.

04

### Invoices and reconciliation

Supplier invoices are matched to orders, so costs and margins are checked without manual entry.

05

### Catalog onboarding

New supplier catalogs are mapped to your products, collections and attributes, ready to rank and sell.

06

### Monitoring and exceptions

Failed documents, stock mismatches and late shipments are flagged so someone can act before a customer notices.

Questions

## EDI integration questions

### What is EDI?

EDI, or electronic data interchange, is a set of standard documents that lets your store and a supplier exchange inventory, purchase orders, ship notices and invoices without manual entry. Both sides send and receive the same formats, so orders and updates move automatically instead of by email or spreadsheet.

### Which documents do you set up?

We usually set up inventory updates (846), purchase orders (850), order acknowledgments (855), ship notices (856) and invoices (810). The exact set depends on what each supplier supports. We document every flow so your team knows which supplier sends what and when.

### What if a supplier does not support EDI?

We connect through their API, an SFTP file feed or a scheduled CSV instead. Every supplier ends up in the same automated flow, so your store sees one consistent stream of stock levels, order confirmations and tracking, whatever format each supplier uses.

### Which platforms do you work on?

We work on Shopify stores connected to wholesale and dropship suppliers. That includes custom apps and middleware that sit between Shopify and each trading partner. If you are moving to Shopify from another platform, we plan the EDI connections as part of the migration.

### How do you measure success?

We measure order accuracy, time from order to supplier, sales lost to stock errors and hours of manual work removed. These are tracked before and after each supplier goes live, so you can see what the integration changed rather than relying on general claims.

URLs and redirects

## How do Magento URLs map to Shopify?

Magento URLs map to Shopify's fixed /products/, /collections/, /pages/ and /blogs/ paths, so almost every URL changes and needs a 301 redirect. Magento lets you set any URL key and suffix; Shopify does not.

### Product pages

/blue-jacket.html or /men/jackets/blue-jacket.html becomes /products/blue-jacket. Each category path version of a product URL gets its own redirect.

### Category pages

/men/jackets.html becomes /collections/mens-jackets. Shopify collections are flat, so nested categories need a menu and filter plan.

### CMS pages and blog posts

/about-us becomes /pages/about-us. Posts from a Magento blog extension move to Shopify blogs at /blogs/news/post-handle.

[All Shopify migrations →](https://www.nativecode.ai/services/shopify-migration)

### Store views and filters

Store view URLs for other countries or languages map to Shopify Markets. Layered navigation filter URLs redirect to the parent collection, not one by one.

FAQ

## Questions about Magento to Shopify migration

### Will we lose SEO rankings moving from Magento to Shopify?

Not if the migration is planned for search. Most ranking losses come from missing redirects, and a Magento store can have thousands of URL rewrites, including .html suffixes and category paths. We map each one to its Shopify URL, carry over titles, meta descriptions and content, and monitor Search Console after launch to catch gaps early.

### Can you migrate Adobe Commerce and Magento 1 stores?

Yes. We migrate Magento 2, Adobe Commerce and Adobe Commerce Cloud stores, and Magento 1 stores still running after Magento 1 reached end of life in June 2020. The data model is similar across versions, so the work is mapping products, attributes, customers and URLs to Shopify, then replacing extensions and integrations.

### What happens to configurable products and custom attributes?

Configurable products become Shopify products with variants, and each child simple product becomes a variant with its own SKU, price and inventory. Shopify allows three options per product, so products with more option attributes need a different structure or an options app. Custom attributes used for specs or filters move to metafields.

### Can customers keep their accounts and order history?

Customer records, addresses and order history can move from Magento to Shopify, but passwords cannot be migrated for security reasons. After launch, customers receive an account invitation so they can set a new password. We import historical orders for reference and reporting and check totals on a staging store first.

### Does Shopify support Magento B2B features and store views?

Largely, through Shopify Plus. Shopify Plus B2B covers company accounts, catalogs with custom pricing, payment terms and quantity rules, which replaces many Adobe Commerce B2B setups. Store views for other countries or languages usually map to Shopify Markets. Features such as requisition lists or complex quote flows may need an app or custom work.

### What happens to our ERP and EDI integrations?

We rebuild them for Shopify before launch. Common ERPs and EDI providers have Shopify connectors, and others can use the Shopify Admin API. We test product, inventory and order flows against the staging store, plan switch-over day so orders keep flowing to your ERP and suppliers, and watch the feeds closely in the weeks after.

Questions

## Marketplace management questions

### Which marketplaces do you manage?

We manage Amazon, Walmart Marketplace and eBay for brands that also sell through their own store. Each marketplace has its own listing rules, fees, account health metrics and ad platform, so we run them as separate channels that share one catalog and one inventory source. Other marketplaces can be added when they fit your products.

### Can you sync our Shopify catalog and inventory to Amazon and Walmart?

Yes. We connect Shopify or your ERP to each marketplace through native integrations, feed tools or custom connections, then map products, variants and attributes to each marketplace's categories. Inventory and orders sync both ways, so stock sold on one channel updates the others and orders reach your fulfillment team or 3PL without manual entry.

### What is the Amazon Buy Box and why does it matter?

The Buy Box is the Add to Cart section on an Amazon product page, and the seller who holds it gets the sale when a shopper clicks Add to Cart. Amazon awards it based on factors such as price, delivery speed, stock and seller performance. We monitor who holds it, fix the issues we can control and set pricing rules that protect your margin.

### Do you run Amazon and Walmart advertising?

Yes. We run Amazon Sponsored Products and Sponsored Brands, Walmart Connect and eBay Promoted Listings. Campaigns are built around your product margins, with separate structures for brand, competitor and category searches. We report advertising cost of sales alongside total sales by channel, so ad spend is judged on profit, not only on ad-attributed revenue.

### How does EDI fit into marketplace management?

EDI moves purchase orders, ship notices, inventory and invoices between you, your suppliers and some retail partners in standard formats. When products sold on Amazon, Walmart or eBay ship from a supplier or 3PL, EDI or API connections keep stock and tracking accurate on every channel. Our EDI integration service builds and monitors those connections.

FAQ

## Questions about Shopify migration

### Will we lose SEO rankings when we migrate to Shopify?

Not if the migration is planned for search. Most ranking losses come from missing or wrong redirects. We map every old URL to its new Shopify URL, carry over titles, content and schema, and monitor Search Console after launch to catch any gaps early.

### How long does a Shopify migration take?

A Shopify migration usually takes a few months. The timing depends on catalog size, data quality and the number of apps and integrations to replace, and stores with EDI or custom features take longer. You get a written timeline before work starts, with launch planned for a low-traffic window.

### What happens to our supplier EDI connections?

We plan EDI continuity as part of the migration, not after it. Supplier, inventory and order connections are rebuilt and tested against the new Shopify store before launch. On switch-over day orders keep flowing to suppliers, and we watch the feeds closely in the first weeks after go-live.

### Can you move customer accounts and order history?

Yes. Customers, order history and gift cards can be migrated to Shopify. Passwords cannot be moved for security reasons, so we set up an account activation email that returning customers receive. We test the data on a staging store first, so totals and order records match before launch.

### Do you migrate from Magento 1 and Magento 2?

Yes. We migrate stores from both Magento 1 and Magento 2, also known as Adobe Commerce, including stores with large catalogs, configurable products and custom URL rewrites. Magento URL patterns differ from Shopify's, so the redirect map is one of the most important parts of the project.

FAQ

## Questions about Shopify Plus

### When does a brand need Shopify Plus?

A brand usually needs Shopify Plus when it needs what standard plans limit or leave out: the full B2B feature set, checkout customization across every step, custom apps built on Shopify Functions, expansion stores, Launchpad, or higher API limits for ERP and 3PL integrations. Sales volume alone is not the reason. We check your requirements during the free store review and tell you if a standard plan still fits.

### What replaced checkout.liquid on Shopify Plus?

Checkout Extensibility replaced checkout.liquid. Shopify has deprecated checkout.liquid, so checkout customizations now use checkout UI extensions, Shopify Functions for discount, shipping and payment logic, checkout branding settings and web pixels for tracking. We audit what your current checkout does, rebuild each customization in the supported model and test it in a development store before switching over.

### Can Shopify Plus handle B2B and wholesale?

Yes. Shopify Plus includes B2B features: company accounts with multiple buyers and locations, catalogs and price lists, payment terms, quantity rules and draft orders. Wholesale buyers can order from the same store as retail customers or from a separate expansion store. We set up the B2B configuration and connect it to your ERP so pricing and orders stay in sync.

### Can you migrate our store to Shopify Plus?

Yes. We migrate stores from Magento, BigCommerce, WooCommerce and Salesforce Commerce Cloud, and upgrade standard Shopify stores to Plus. Products, customers, orders and content move over, every URL gets a 301 redirect and SEO elements carry across, all planned to protect search traffic. Our Magento to Shopify migration page covers the process in detail.

### Do you connect Shopify Plus to ERP, 3PL and EDI systems?

Yes. We connect Shopify Plus to ERPs such as NetSuite, to 3PL warehouses and to retail partners over EDI, so orders, inventory, shipments and invoices move without manual entry. We use the Shopify Admin API, webhooks and middleware where it fits, and we monitor the connections after launch so failed syncs are caught and fixed quickly.

    ### Audit

    Crawl the Squarespace site and list every URL, product, customer export and feature in use.
